changes.before: What were you hoping to see instead?
changes.after: How does the output compare with what you expected?

changes.before: Would it help to identify one observation that would strengthen confidence in the result?
changes.after: Would it help to identify one observation that could increase or decrease your confidence in the result?

changes.before: What does everyone think is most important right now?
changes.after: From your perspective, what matters most right now?

changes.before: Understand expected and actual results before proposing a fix. Requested direct assistance is welcome; do not withhold it to prolong questioning. This is optional: adapt, decline, request direct help, or choose another next step. AI self-critique is not proof; use evidence suited to the consequence, not exhaustive human auditing.
changes.after: Test one reversible step, if wanted: compare expected and actual results. If mistakes could harm people or real work, use a copy or mock-up; stop before those effects. One result informs only that step. Give requested direct help; adapt, decline or continue human-only. AI/tools may check observations; AI self-critique is not proof. Match evidence to consequences, not exhaustive human re-auditing.

changes.before: Explore differences without forcing a winner. Keeping a human-only approach is a complete choice. This is optional: adapt, decline, request direct help, or choose another next step. AI self-critique is not proof; use evidence suited to the consequence, not exhaustive human auditing.
changes.after: Sketch, say or draw one feasible human-only step; that is a complete choice. Only if useful, compare realistic human-only, AI-assisted and hybrid routes: preparation, work, checking, correction, integration and learning and capability. No winner or AI trial is required. Adapt, decline or request direct help. AI/tools may check feasibility against sources or observations; AI self-critique is not proof. Match evidence to consequences, not exhaustive human re-auditing.

changes.before: Understand expected versus actual results before changing prompts. The goal, context, data, tool limits or choice to use AI may matter. Only if they report disappointing output, you could ask: What part felt least useful? This is optional: adapt, decline, request direct help, or choose another next step. AI self-critique is not proof; use evidence suited to the consequence, not exhaustive human auditing.
changes.after: Compare expectations and output; consider goal, context, data, tool limits or choosing AI. Only if disappointing, ask what felt least useful. If wanted, check one consequential claim against original sources, executed checks or observations; AI/tools can help. Missing evidence leaves uncertainty. Adapt, decline, request direct help or continue human-only. AI self-critique is not proof. Match evidence to consequences, not exhaustive human re-auditing.

changes.before: Differences can remain visible. Do not invent agreement or diagnose silence. Offer passing, writing, drawing, spoken or paired alternatives; sharing is optional. This is optional: adapt, decline, request direct help, or choose another next step. AI self-critique is not proof; use evidence suited to the consequence, not exhaustive human auditing.
changes.after: Listen for differences; do not diagnose silence or infer agreement from silence or sharing. Quiet thinking, writing or drawing is optional; offer spoken or paired alternatives. Passing needs no explanation. Sharing is voluntary; nothing needs collecting. Adapt, decline, request direct help or continue human-only. If checking a shared claim, AI/tools may use sources or observations; AI self-critique is not proof. Match evidence to consequences, not exhaustive human re-auditing.
